findings.issue: replacedStylesOption compares each run seat's style to the preset's; since a replacement now keeps its style (and a violation resets to the preset), the 'changed' branch can never be true in a real playtest run, so the function always returns ''.
findings.evidence: runner.ts:384-389 now copies the busted seat's own style; the re-pinned tests/playtest/replacement.acceptance.test.ts asserts the Replay line ends with ' --lineup mixed' and no --styles. cli.ts is not in the spec's file list, so leaving it is within scope, but it is now effectively dead code with a doc comment that describes behaviour that no longer occurs.
findings.fix: Follow-up (or here if the orchestrator extends the file list): delete replacedStylesOption and its call at cli.ts:310, and adjust the cli.test.ts:686 title/assertion that exercises it through a seam. Keep stylesOption for the --styles replay echo (A-7).

findings.issue: The CO raise justification says the Rock 'adds medium pairs and suited broadway hands', but the additions also include AJo (offsuit), and AQo was already present; the sentence undersells the range REQ-026.3 asks justifications to describe truthfully.
findings.evidence: Added classes per spec §5: KQs KJs 99 88 AJo QJs. AJo is offsuit.
findings.fix: Reword to e.g. 'adds medium pairs down to eights and more broadway hands, suited and ace-jack offsuit, and still folds every weaker hand.'

findings.issue: The fold->call justification ends 'keeps its aggression from reaching every street', which is hard to parse; the real effect is that calls (not bets/raises) lower its postflop aggression into its 65-85 band.
findings.evidence: Spec §1a: without this the Maniac's AGG was 94.2-94.6 because it 'almost never calls'.
findings.fix: Replace the last clause with 'and the extra calls keep its postflop aggression inside its 65 to 85 percent band'.

findings.issue: tally() still runs nextHand over 10,000 replay codes although the style no longer depends on the code; it confirms code-independence but costs runtime and the 'drawn'/'tally' names now describe a draw that no longer exists.
findings.evidence: Kept to preserve the locked file's check structure (one-for-one re-pin).
findings.fix: Acceptable as is for the re-pin; optionally rename drawn() to keptStyles() in a later unlocked edit.

summary: All seven SPEC items are implemented as specified. Replacement keeps current.style in both nextHand (session.ts:558) and runPlaytest (runner.ts:384); drawReplacementStyle, replacementStyles and replacementGenerator plus the 'No replay code' throw are gone with no remaining references in src/tests/docs. Session-record format is untouched (style field still stored per seat), so older records still load. maniac.json and rock.json match spec §5 exactly (call->raise 0.2, fold->call 0.8, check->bet 0.6; Rock bar 80; range additions give the re-pinned COUNTS 13/16/21, 13/16, 17). REQ-007.5/007.7/007.8 and changelog 1.11 match the code (Custom included, per A-2). Locked re-pins replace values one-for-one; deleted random-draw checks became same-style checks (lineup.test, replacement.acceptance, next-hand, replace-bot, session-records, playtest replacement), and maniac.acceptance adds the SPEC-05 boundary checks (draw just under/at 0.8). The new mixed-composition test would fail under a random redraw: it asserts the 5-bot style multiset on all 2,000 hands, per-replacement before/after style equality, and an app nextHand with four busted bots of mixed styles at Custom and Mixed tables. Reviewer re-ran the five key test files (pass) and the SPEC-06 SHA (match). No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings; two MINOR (dead replacedStylesOption branch in cli.ts outside spec file list; Rock CO justification omits AJo) and two NITs.
